breaking_changes.BC_description: Node.js 0.10.x and 0.12.x are no longer supported. Projects running on these Node versions will fail to use this library.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Upgrade your Node.js runtime to at least v4.x or higher to use v2.0.0 of node-fetch.

breaking_changes.BC_description: Directly requiring internal modules like 'node-fetch/lib/response' is now unsupported. Instead, you must use 'require('node-fetch').Response' for CommonJS, or ES6 import syntax.
The 'response.text()' method now always returns text as UTF-8 without attempting to detect encoding. For the previous behavior, 'response.textConverted()' should be used.
response.json() now throws an error on HTTP 204 No Content response instead of returning an empty object.

Internal methods of node-fetch are no longer exposed. Any code that imported and used undocumented internal methods will break. In v1.x, the user can access internal methods such as '_clone()', '_decode()', and '_convert()' on the 'response' object. In v2.x, these methods are completely inaccessible.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Remove all usages of undocumented/internal APIs from node-fetch/lib/*. Use only public, documented APIs exposed in the main 'node-fetch' module.
breaking_changes.RequireInfo: Precise enumeration of which internal methods were previously accessible and now are not is needed to fully enumerate affected APIs for downstream clients.

breaking_changes.BC_description: An error is now thrown when constructing a Request object with a GET or HEAD method and a non-null body, following the specification.
The 'headers.getAll()' method is removed. 'headers.get()' now returns all matching header values joined by comma, per spec.
The Headers 'get()' method now returns all matching header values joined by a comma string (not just the first match). Previous behavior can be emulated with 'get().split(',')[0]'.
All method parameters for Headers methods are now stringified. This means set/get/delete methods (and others) automatically convert non-string arguments to strings.

Invalid HTTP header names and values are now rejected outright by Headers methods and constructor. Attempting to set/get headers with invalid (non-ASCII or illegal) characters now throws an error. This applies both when constructing Headers and when using instance methods (append, delete, get, has, set), whereas previously such headers may have been accepted or handled differently.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Audit all locations in the codebase where headers are constructed or manipulated. Ensure header names use only valid characters. Avoid spaces or non-ASCII in header names. Catch or prevent potential TypeErrors when manipulating headers and validate input before use.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Headers constructor now throws a TypeError when initialized with any value that is not a tuple, or with non-iterable or incorrectly shaped iterable values. This introduces stricter validation of headers input, making formerly accepted values (like solitary strings, objects with non-iterable iterators, or arrays with extra elements) invalid.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Ensure that all usages of the Headers constructor provide an iterable of 2-element arrays (tuples) or a valid plain object. Review all code where Headers is instantiated, and update parameters that may now cause a TypeError (such as single strings, objects with invalid iterator symbols, or arrays with more than two elements per entry) to adhere to this stricter expectation.

breaking_changes.BC_description: Selected attributes ('body', 'bodyUsed', 'method', 'url', 'headers', 'redirect') of the Request class are now enforced as read-only. Attempts to assign a value to these properties will throw an exception, reflecting a behavioral breaking change if they were previously writable.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Refactor code to avoid direct assignment to these properties. If property values must be modified, create a new Request instance with the desired attributes, or use provided methods for safe data access and mutation.
